title: Parabolic Short
teaches: The parabolic short as we trade it: a stock that has already run far goes vertical for 3 to 5 days, gaps up on the climax day on record volume, and is shorted at market only after it cracks back under VWAP; the stop sits a few cents over the day's high, the size comes from that wide stop, the target is the daily 9 EMA within a few sessions, and a reclaim of the high, a passed window or a squeeze through the 2R gap ceiling ends it.

facts.quote: Two days of volume expansion, with each day's volume higher than the last.
facts.claim: Bracco's fourth box: two days of rising volume.

steps: GDS, February 2025. A 13-session run from a flat base, up 145%, four of four boxes.

The trigger lives on the 5-minute chart: the break under VWAP after the high. Our daily stand-in is the red close, 48.50.
Stop a few cents over the day's high, 52.56. Target the daily 9 EMA: reached in 2 sessions, 3R on day 5.

questions.q: In one line, what is a Parabolic Short?
choices: A short of a vertical run as it cracks
A short of any stock under its 200-day
A short at the top before the crack
A long bought on a crash day
questions.answer: A short of a vertical run as it cracks
questions.why: A short of a vertical run as it cracks. Bracco: the burst is a 3-5 day move, the final leg of a parabolic run. A mean-reversion trade, not always a lasting top.
questions.lesson_line: You short the crack of a vertical run, never the run itself.

wrong.A short of any stock under its 200-day: This setup lives far above its 200-day, in one of the hottest stocks in the market.
wrong.A short at the top before the crack: Nobody knows the top. We short after the intraday trend turns, not before.
wrong.A long bought on a crash day: That is the Parabolic Long, the mirror image.

questions.q: Our rule says no shorts above the 200-day. Why may this one be shorted there?
choices: B26's parabolic exception
Any short is fine once a stock is up 50%
No exception; wait for the 200-day
Only in a Red market
questions.answer: B26's parabolic exception
questions.why: B26 names the parabolic short as its one exception. Shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short, as Bracco's post defines it.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day there is one short we take, and Bracco's post says what it is.

wrong.Any short is fine once a stock is up 50%: A percent gain is not the test. The exception is the parabolic burst, by Bracco's definition.
wrong.No exception; wait for the 200-day: Waiting for the 200-day means missing the whole trade. The rule carves out this one case.
wrong.Only in a Red market: The market reading is not what lets it through. The parabolic definition is.

questions.q: Bracco will not take the climax-day short without a gap up on the climax day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. In his words: you never know exactly when the climax day will hit, but he won't short without that gap-up. Our card requires it too.
questions.lesson_line: No gap up, no climax-day short.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The target of a Parabolic Short is the daily ___ EMA.
questions.why: 9. The target is the daily 9 EMA. Bracco calls it a magnet for mean reversion, and our rule names it as this setup's target.
questions.lesson_line: The trade runs to the 9 EMA. Know where it sits before you short.

questions.q: Where does the stop sit on a Parabolic Short?
choices: A few cents over the day's high
A few cents under the day's low
At the 9 EMA, below the price
A fixed 3% above your fill price
questions.answer: A few cents over the day's high
questions.why: A few cents over the day's high. Bracco's thesis is that the top is in, so the day's high is the line. Kullamagi: the stop is the highs of the day.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is over the day's high. If that goes, the top was not in.

wrong.A few cents under the day's low: That is a long's stop. A short's stop sits above price.
wrong.At the 9 EMA, below the price: The 9 EMA is the target, not the stop. A short's stop sits above price.
wrong.A fixed 3% above your fill price: The stop is a level on the chart, the day's high, not a percent.

questions.q: On the climax day you short the gap up at the open, before the high is set.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. After the gap up, nothing at the open. Shorting at the day's highs is a dangerous trap; let the amateur shorts get run over first.
questions.lesson_line: The open is for watching. The crack is for shorting.

questions.q: Which of these is one of Bracco's burst boxes?
choices: Two straight overnight gap ups
A close under the 50-day
Volume falling two days running
A ten-week base before the run
questions.answer: Two straight overnight gap ups
questions.why: Two straight overnight gap ups. The boxes: three straight up days, two gap ups, two of three days of bigger gains, two days of rising volume. Plus a gap up on the climax day.
questions.lesson_line: Count the boxes: up days, gap ups, bigger gains, rising volume, the climax gap.

wrong.A close under the 50-day: A burst runs far above its averages. A close under the 50-day is a different chart.
wrong.Volume falling two days running: The box is rising volume, each day higher than the last.
wrong.A ten-week base before the run: The boxes count the burst's last days, not the base before it.

questions.q: The climax day gaps up, runs higher for 20 minutes, then turns. What is the first entry?
choices: The break back under VWAP
The opening print
The first green 5-minute bar
A daily close under the 9 EMA
questions.answer: The break back under VWAP
questions.why: The break back under VWAP. Bracco: 10 to 60 minutes in, sellers emerge; the first entry is a breakdown below VWAP. He never enters before that.
questions.lesson_line: The first entry is the VWAP break after the high is set.

wrong.The opening print: Nothing at the open. The high is not set yet.
wrong.The first green 5-minute bar: A green bar is strength. The entry is the break down, under VWAP.
wrong.A daily close under the 9 EMA: The 9 EMA is where the trade ends, not where it starts.

questions.q: On daily bars, the stand-in for the intraday crack is a climax day that closes above its open.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Bracco's favorite shape is a final gap up that opens higher and closes lower. On daily bars that red close stands in for the VWAP break.
questions.lesson_line: Opens higher, closes lower: that is the crack on a daily chart.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Bracco's parabolic burst is the final leg of a run, lasting ___ to 5 days.
questions.why: 3. Bracco: the parabolic burst is a 3-5 day move that marks the final leg. In his studies most bursts last 3 to 5 days.
questions.lesson_line: The burst is short: three to five days, then the gap.

questions.q: By Kullamagi's rule, how far has a larger-cap stock run before it is a candidate?
choices: 50% to 100% or more in days or weeks
5% to 10% in a month
300% to 1,000% or more
The run does not matter; the gap does
questions.answer: 50% to 100% or more in days or weeks
questions.why: 50% to 100% or more in days or weeks. Kullamagi's floor for a larger cap; smaller caps need 300% to 1,000% or more. Our card takes 50% for large caps.
questions.lesson_line: A big run comes first. Half again its price, at least, in days or weeks.

wrong.5% to 10% in a month: That is a normal month, not a parabolic run.
wrong.300% to 1,000% or more: That is his floor for a smaller cap, not a larger one.
wrong.The run does not matter; the gap does: The gap ends a run. Without the large advance there is nothing to exhaust.

questions.q: Is this our Parabolic Short?
choices: No; week one out of a base
Yes; the gap and red close make it
Yes, at half size
questions.answer: No; week one out of a base
questions.why: No. A stock in week one out of a long base is not this setup; Bracco calls that trade very short lived. RGTI did the same and made a new high six sessions later.
questions.lesson_line: A stock just out of a base has fuel left. Let it run.

wrong.Yes; the gap and red close make it: The daily shape fits, the context does not. Three days out of a base is not an exhausted run.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Size does not fix the wrong setup. It is a pass.

questions.story: A stock broke out of a six-month base three days ago. Two up days, then today it gaps up 4% and closes red.

questions.q: A hard-to-borrow stock with a high borrow fee is skipped, even on a perfect climax day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Skip a short when the stock is hard to borrow or the fee is high. Kullamagi has expensive locates most retail brokers do not; most of us do not.
questions.lesson_line: No borrow, no trade. The chart does not pay the fee.

questions.q: The VWAP break prints. What order do you send?
choices: A market order, now
A limit a few cents lower
A sell-stop under the day's low
Wait for the 5-minute close
questions.answer: A market order, now
questions.why: A market order, now. Entries are market orders. The level has printed and the stop is already known, so there is nothing to wait for.
questions.lesson_line: When the trigger prints, you are in at market.

wrong.A limit a few cents lower: A limit under the print can miss the whole first leg down.
wrong.A sell-stop under the day's low: That is Bracco's second entry, which we do not take. One entry, at the VWAP break.
wrong.Wait for the 5-minute close: The bar closing is not the trigger. The trade under VWAP is.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Out; the high is reclaimed
Hold; it is only a few cents
Widen the stop to 54.00
Add; the thesis still holds
questions.answer: Out; the high is reclaimed
questions.why: Out. If the price reclaims the day's high, the thesis or the timing was wrong, and you exit. The stop is the exit; it never widens.
questions.lesson_line: The day's high is the line. Over it, you are wrong, and wrong is flat.

wrong.Hold; it is only a few cents: A few cents over the high is over the high. A new high means the top was not in.
wrong.Widen the stop to 54.00: The stop never widens. Parabolic advances go further than anyone thinks.
wrong.Add; the thesis still holds: Bracco never adds when he is down. Neither do we.

questions.story: You shorted the VWAP break at 48.50 with the stop over the high at 52.56. At 2 pm it trades 52.60.

questions.q: On the climax day, what should the volume look like?
choices: The highest of the whole run
Lighter than the day before
Average; volume does not matter
Heavy only in the last hour
questions.answer: The highest of the whole run
questions.why: The highest of the whole run. Bracco: the climax day almost invariably shows the highest opening volume of the entire run. A big spike after a massive move signals exhaustion.
questions.lesson_line: The crowd buys the top. Record volume on the climax day is the tell.

wrong.Lighter than the day before: Lighter volume is not a climax. The card wants a record; rising but not a record is only a B- mark.
wrong.Average; volume does not matter: Volume is half of Bracco's first two checks: range and volume expansion.
wrong.Heavy only in the last hour: The record volume comes at the open, in the first minutes of the gap.

questions.q: A stock that climbed in steady stair-steps for a year is a Parabolic Short once it is up 100%.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A steady, controlled ascent is the one to avoid; it reflects strength and can persist. Judging by percent gain alone is a frequent mistake.
questions.lesson_line: Percent gain is not the test. Shape is. Stair-steps are not a parabola.

questions.q: Short the VWAP break today?
choices: No; a report inside 3 sessions
Yes; the setup triggered today
Yes; a report helps the crack
Yes, at half the usual size
questions.answer: No; a report inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new short within 3 sessions of a report. A gap through the stop on earnings is a risk no setup grade buys back.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings inside three days is a pass, however good the chart.

wrong.Yes; the setup triggered today: The trigger fired and the calendar still says no. The earnings rule is a hard line.
wrong.Yes; a report helps the crack: A report is a gap you cannot stop, in either direction.
wrong.Yes, at half the usual size: Size does not fix report risk. Smaller is still in.

questions.story: The burst is textbook and the climax day gaps up 9%. Earnings come after the close tomorrow.

questions.q: The prior close is 42.00 and the climax day opens at 48.47. How big is the gap up, in percent?
questions.why: 15.4%. The open over the prior close, minus one. A gap of 5% or more is stronger; GDS gapped 15.4% on record volume and closed red.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap in percent. Big gaps on record volume are the best climaxes.

questions.q: Stopped out of the climax short on Tuesday. Wednesday it cracks under VWAP again. Allowed?
choices: Yes; a new trigger in the window
No; one try per climax move
Yes; keep the stop from Tuesday
No; never re-short the same climax run
questions.answer: Yes; a new trigger in the window
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, a new trigger is a new trade with its own stop. The window is 1 to 2 days; at most 3 tries in a week.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict. The next trigger is a new trade, inside the window.

wrong.No; one try per climax move: The cap is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one.
wrong.Yes; keep the stop from Tuesday: A new trade has its own stop: over the new day's high at entry.
wrong.No; never re-short the same climax run: Stamatoudis gives it a 1 to 2-day window, and so do we. After that, drop it.

questions.q: We short parabolic names only at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. A climax in a thin stock is a halt waiting to happen.
questions.lesson_line: Liquidity first. A thin stock can squeeze through any stop.

questions.q: Tap the name that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Bracco's favorite climax-day pattern, a run at the open then a break under VWAP, is the ___.
questions.answer: U-Turn
questions.why: The U-Turn. Bracco's preferred intraday pattern: the gap runs higher, then 10 to 60 minutes in sellers emerge and it breaks under VWAP. Our A+ row.
questions.lesson_line: A run at the open, then a fast break under VWAP: the U-Turn.

questions.q: By Bracco, when is a Parabolic Short complete?
choices: At the 9 EMA test on the backside
When it falls 50% from the high
When it closes under the 200-day
The next morning, whatever happens
questions.answer: At the 9 EMA test on the backside
questions.why: At the 9 EMA test on the backside of the move. That is his target and our rule's target.
questions.lesson_line: The trade is done at the 9 EMA. Do not wait for a crash.

wrong.When it falls 50% from the high: Some do, most do not. The 9 EMA is the target, and it is usually close.
wrong.When it closes under the 200-day: The stock sits far above its 200-day. That is weeks away, if ever.
wrong.The next morning, whatever happens: Time is not the target. The 9 EMA is; it often comes within a day or two.

questions.q: The prior close is 48.50 and the 9-day EMA sits at 40.00. How far above the average is the close, in percent?
questions.why: 21.25%. The close over the average, minus one. Read a chart in percents: Bracco's checklist lists % extensions from moving averages and ATR multiples from the 50-day.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stretch in percent before you call anything parabolic.

questions.q: Shorted at 29.66 with the stop at 31.81. How wide is the stop, in percent of the fill?
questions.why: 7.25%. The stop minus the fill, over the fill. Wider than the 3% our stops usually sit within, so the shares shrink: the size comes from the stop. That was BILI.
questions.lesson_line: A wide stop is allowed. A big position on a wide stop is not.

questions.q: Account 50,000. Risk 0.5%. Short 48.50, stop 52.56. How many shares?
questions.why: 61. Account times risk percent, divided by the stop minus the fill, rounded down. Stop first, size last; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last. The same on the short side.

questions.q: Short it now?
choices: No; wait for the break under VWAP
Yes; the gap is the trigger
Yes; a small starter short here
No; never short into a gap-up day
questions.answer: No; wait for the break under VWAP
questions.why: No. After the gap up, nothing at the open. Shorting at the day's highs is a dangerous trap; Stamatoudis would rather miss the move than be chopped up by early attempts.
questions.lesson_line: The crowd screaming top is not a trigger. The VWAP break is.

wrong.Yes; the gap is the trigger: The gap is the setup. The trigger is the break under VWAP after the high is set.
wrong.Yes; a small starter short here: Small and early is still early. Let the amateur shorts get run over first.
wrong.No; never short into a gap-up day: A gap up that cracks is exactly this trade. The timing is the point, not the gap.

questions.story: The climax day gaps up 9% and runs higher in the first 10 minutes. Everyone is calling the top.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
choices: 53.40, the first 30-minute high
Cover at the open, 53.00
Keep 52.56; it was the rule
Get out; the gap is past 2R
questions.answer: 53.40, the first 30-minute high
questions.why: 53.40. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute bar. Its high is the new stop, with a ceiling of 2R; 53.40 is inside that ceiling.
questions.lesson_line: A gap over the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Cover at the open, 53.00: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The open is not the decision.
wrong.Keep 52.56; it was the rule: Price is already through it. The gap rule replaces it with the 30-minute high.
wrong.Get out; the gap is past 2R: 53.40 is inside the 2R ceiling. The ceiling has not been hit.

questions.story: Short at 48.50, stop 52.56. Next morning it gaps open at 53.00, through your stop. The first 30-minute bar's high is 53.40.

questions.q: We add a second short at the break of the day's low, as Bracco does.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Bracco's first entry is the VWAP break, followed by a second at the day's lows. Our rule: the full size at one price with one stop; the second entry is not taught.
questions.lesson_line: One entry, one stop, full size. That is the whole position.

questions.q: Short it here?
choices: No; more than 4% under the break
Yes; the crack is confirmed and clean
Yes; half size is safer here
Yes, with the stop at 50.00
questions.answer: No; more than 4% under the break
questions.why: No. 47.50 sits more than 4% under the 50.00 break. No chasing: our 4% limit mirrored for a short. The stop stays over the high, so a late fill shrinks the reward.
questions.lesson_line: I would rather miss it than chase it. Four percent and done, both ways.

wrong.Yes; the crack is confirmed and clean: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Yes; half size is safer here: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry.
wrong.Yes, with the stop at 50.00: A stop under the day's high is a stop inside the noise. The stop is over the high.

questions.story: The VWAP break printed at 50.00 while you were away. Now it trades 47.50, still well above the 9 EMA.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: In a parabolic run the pauses get ___ as the price goes higher.
questions.answer: shorter
questions.why: Shorter. Bracco: ideally the consolidation periods shorten as the price surges higher, with minimal pullbacks. Each pause shorter, each pullback smaller, the ATR rising.
questions.lesson_line: Parabolic means the rests get shorter. Linear means they do not.

questions.q: Short the close?
choices: No; a green day, no crack
Yes; the burst must be done
Yes; tomorrow will gap down
questions.answer: No; a green day, no crack
questions.why: No. On daily bars the crack is a close under the open; shorting a green climax day won 23% of the time. Here the real top came the next day and a short at that close was stopped at 0R.
questions.lesson_line: A green climax day has not cracked. Strength is not a trigger.

wrong.Yes; the burst must be done: Nobody knows the burst is done until it cracks. Green at the close means it has not.
wrong.Yes; tomorrow will gap down: Maybe. A guess about tomorrow is not a trigger today.

questions.story: After a five-day burst the stock gaps up and never looks back. It closes 15.8% above its open, near the top of its range.

questions.q: Two climax days. One: four boxes, a 15% gap, record volume. The other: two boxes, a 2% gap, average volume. Which grades higher?
choices: The four-box day with the big gap
The two-box day; quieter is safer
Equal; only the crack counts
questions.answer: The four-box day with the big gap
questions.why: The four-box day. The more boxes checked, the stronger. All 4 boxes plus a gap of 5% or more is our A+ row; record volume is the A+ volume row.
questions.lesson_line: More boxes, a bigger gap, a record crowd: that is the five-star climax.

wrong.The two-box day; quieter is safer: Quiet is not safe here. A small gap and average volume is the B- row.
wrong.Equal; only the crack counts: The crack is the trigger. The boxes, the gap and the volume are the grade.

questions.q: Which of Bracco's intraday patterns is that, and how does he grade it?
choices: Long-drawn-out breakdown; 3 or 4 stars
The U-Turn; his favorite
Quick opening range breakdown; 5 stars
questions.answer: Long-drawn-out breakdown; 3 or 4 stars
questions.why: The Long-Drawn-Out Range Breakdown: a tight range for the first one to two hours. Bracco sees it more often in 3 or 4-star setups that do not fully meet all criteria.
questions.lesson_line: A clean U-Turn is five stars. Two hours of chop first is not.

wrong.The U-Turn; his favorite: The U-Turn turns 10 to 60 minutes in. Two hours of range is the drawn-out version.
wrong.Quick opening range breakdown; 5 stars: That one sets its high on the first 5-minute candle. And it is his least liked, not five stars.

questions.story: The climax day gaps up, then chops in a tight range for two hours before breaking under VWAP.

questions.q: If the short is held, the stop moves to breakeven at 2R; on this setup the 9 EMA usually comes first.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Breakeven at 2R to 5R ideally, as on any trade. For this setup the 9 EMA cover usually comes first, so breakeven rarely matters.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven at 2R, if the 9 EMA has not already ended the trade.

questions.q: By our card, what now?
choices: Cover; three sessions, no 9 EMA
Hold; the stop is a long way off
Add; it has not squeezed
Hold until the 10-day time stop
questions.answer: Cover; three sessions, no 9 EMA
questions.why: Cover. If the 9 EMA is not reached within 3 sessions of entry, cover; the 10-day time stop is only the outer limit. TSLA touched it on day 8, above the entry, then chopped 25 sessions to the stop.
questions.lesson_line: This trade pays fast or not at all. Three sessions without the 9 EMA is the exit.

wrong.Hold; the stop is a long way off: A far stop is a reason for fewer shares, not for waiting. The time limit has run out.
wrong.Add; it has not squeezed: Never add to a parabolic short. Not squeezed yet is not a reason.
wrong.Hold until the 10-day time stop: The 10-day rule is the outer limit for any trade. This setup's own limit is 3 sessions.

questions.story: You shorted at 99.80, stop 119.80. Three sessions later the 9 EMA is still not reached and the stock chops under its high.

questions.q: You shorted the climax close; the 9 EMA sits only 0.14R away. What is the right yardstick for this trade?
choices: The 9 EMA target, not 3R
3R, as on every other setup
The 50-day average as the target
questions.answer: The 9 EMA target, not 3R
questions.why: The 9 EMA. Our rule names it as this setup's target. MSTR never gave more than 0.77R before chopping: a trade the cover rule handles and a 3R test cannot.
questions.lesson_line: The target is a level, not a multiple. When the level is close, the trade is small.

wrong.3R, as on every other setup: 3R was never on the table. The 9 EMA sits 0.14R away; past it the stock chopped.
wrong.The 50-day average as the target: The 50-day is far below a climax. Bracco's target is the 9 EMA.

questions.q: What is the lesson?
choices: A first climax may not be the last
Never short a mania like this
The stop was too tight for a mania
Hold through the new high next time
questions.answer: A first climax may not be the last
questions.why: The first climax of a mania is not always the last. The 9 EMA came on day 2 at 0.52R, the cover rule's exit; the new high on day 3 took the stop. The window and the three-tries cap limit the damage.
questions.lesson_line: A mania can top twice. Take the 9 EMA, respect the stop, and do not chase the next one.

wrong.Never short a mania like this: Manias are where this setup lives. The lesson is about the window, not the setup.
wrong.The stop was too tight for a mania: A few cents over the climax high is the rule. A new high means the top was not in.
wrong.Hold through the new high next time: Over the high you are wrong. A squeeze from there is a 4R to 5R loss.

questions.story: Shorted 60.68, stop 65.34. Day 2 touches the 9 EMA at 0.52R. Day 3 prints a new high and takes the stop. Twenty sessions later the stock is 27.7% higher.

questions.q: Once short, if the stock reclaims the climax day's high you may give it room by moving the stop higher.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The stop is the exit; it never widens. Bracco: if the price reclaims the day's high, the thesis or the timing was wrong, and he exits.
questions.lesson_line: Room is how a planned loss becomes a disaster. Over the high, you are out.

questions.q: SLV, AGQ and SIVR all hit the climax scan on the same day. What does our card say about commodity ETFs?
choices: A cue against; all three lost
A+; three at once is confirmation
Short the most liquid one only
questions.answer: A cue against; all three lost
questions.why: A cue against. All three hit the scan the same day and all lost on the next leg up. Bracco's own AGQ short failed 3 times over 2 sessions that month.
questions.lesson_line: A commodity in a frenzy does not care about your climax day.

wrong.A+; three at once is confirmation: Three tickers on one metal is one trade, and it lost three times over.
wrong.Short the most liquid one only: Liquidity was not the problem. The next leg up was.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Out; the VWAP reclaim ends it
Hold until 33.40 is reclaimed
Add; VWAP is noise
questions.answer: Out; the VWAP reclaim ends it
questions.why: Out. A VWAP reclaim after a VWAP-fail entry is the exit. Kullamagi: the stop is the highs of the day, or if VWAP fails, a reclaim of the VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: You entered on the failed bounce at VWAP. A reclaim of VWAP says the bounce did not fail.

wrong.Hold until 33.40 is reclaimed: The day's high is the stop for a VWAP-break entry. For a VWAP-fail entry the reclaim is the exit.
wrong.Add; VWAP is noise: VWAP is the one intraday line Kullamagi uses. A reclaim is the thesis failing, not noise.

questions.story: You shorted a failed bounce into VWAP at 31.20; the day's high is 33.40. An hour later it closes a 5-minute bar back over VWAP.

questions.q: What is it?
choices: A News Failure shape, no burst
A Parabolic Short
A Wedge Drop
A Parabolic Long
questions.answer: A News Failure shape, no burst
questions.why: A News Failure shape. A good-news gap up that closes red with no burst before it; a Parabolic Short needs the 3-5 day burst first. AAOI ran 2.16R, then stopped.
questions.lesson_line: Same candle, different setup. Look at the days before the gap.

wrong.A Parabolic Short: No burst, no parabola. The slow drift before the gap is the tell.
wrong.A Wedge Drop: A Wedge Drop comes days after a top, at the averages, under the 200-day.
wrong.A Parabolic Long: That is a burst down and a gap down. This gapped up.

questions.story: A stock drifted up slowly for weeks. Today it gaps up 27.7% on news and closes red. No three straight up closes, no acceleration before it.

questions.q: Our card's read?
choices: Not parabolic; ranges did not expand
Parabolic; the red close is the crack
A+; three weeks of range
questions.answer: Not parabolic; ranges did not expand
questions.why: Not parabolic. The last weekly ranges must each be larger than the one before; the middle week shrank. Consecutive weeks of range expansion is Bracco's mark. NVDA gave 1.19R, then stopped.
questions.lesson_line: A leader's one bad day is not a climax. The weeks before it decide.

wrong.Parabolic; the red close is the crack: The crack only matters on a parabolic run. This run was linear.
wrong.A+; three weeks of range: Three weeks of range is not three weeks of expanding range. The middle week shrank.

questions.story: A steady leader at highs. The last three weekly ranges were 12.33, 5.27 and 13.33 points: the middle week shrank. Today it gaps up and closes red.

questions.q: A 4-day burst ends in a gap on day 5 and the day reverses. The burst ran DOWN. Which trade is it?
choices: The Parabolic Long, on the turn up
The Parabolic Short, on the crack
No trade; a burst runs up, not down
questions.answer: The Parabolic Long, on the turn up
questions.why: The Parabolic Long. The mirror image: a burst down, a gap down on the climax day, bought on the intraday turn. The stop sits under the low and the 9 EMA above.
questions.lesson_line: Look which way the burst went. Down means the long, with everything flipped.

wrong.The Parabolic Short, on the crack: A short needs a burst up and a gap up. This burst ran down.
wrong.No trade; a burst runs up, not down: Our rule has the parabolic long as the mirror image, a burst down.

questions.q: Which setup is that?
choices: A Wedge Drop, days after the top
A Parabolic Short on the climax day
A Parabolic Long
questions.answer: A Wedge Drop, days after the top
questions.why: A Wedge Drop. It comes days later, after a 3 to 10 day stall at the 10-day EMA, and only below the 200-day. A Parabolic Short is taken on the climax day itself.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the distance from the averages. The climax is far from them; the Wedge Drop sits on them.

wrong.A Parabolic Short on the climax day: The climax day is far above the averages. This stock is sitting on them, days later.
wrong.A Parabolic Long: A long needs a burst down and a gap down. This is a stall after a bounce.

questions.story: A stock under its 200-day topped days ago, then stalled five days at its 10-day EMA. Today it broke down out of that stall.

questions.q: Short 521.70, stop 565.54, the 9 EMA at 455.00. How many R is the cover at the 9 EMA?
questions.why: 1.52R. The fill minus the target, over the stop minus the fill. That is the whole reward on this setup.
questions.lesson_line: Count the target in R before you short. The 9 EMA is the trade's reward.

questions.q: The stop over the climax high is usually wider than 3%, so the share count shrinks. The stop is never pulled in to fit.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our stops usually sit within about 3%; here the climax high is often further. The size comes from the stop, and if the honest stop does not fit, skip.
questions.lesson_line: You never pick a size and back-fit a stop under the day's high.

questions.q: Our rule?
choices: No adding; one entry, one stop
Add half; improve your average
Add only if volume dries up fast
questions.answer: No adding; one entry, one stop
questions.why: No adding. The full size at one price with one stop. Bracco: parabolic advances often go further than anyone thinks, so he never adds when he is down.
questions.lesson_line: Averaging up a short is how a 1R loss becomes a blow-up.

wrong.Add half; improve your average: A better average with a bigger position is a bigger squeeze.
wrong.Add only if volume dries up fast: No condition opens the door. One entry, one stop, and the stop decides.

questions.story: Your short is 1R against you, still under the day's high. A friend says average up, the top is in.

questions.q: Which context grades a climax higher, by our card?
choices: Thursday or Friday into expiration
The first day of a new rally
A quiet market with no hype
A stock in week one out of a base
questions.answer: Thursday or Friday into expiration
questions.why: A Thursday or Friday into monthly expiration. Bracco: these moves often peak or unwind then, as a squeeze fades. A stretched index and a cycle ending with leaders going parabolic are the same cue.
questions.lesson_line: The best climaxes come when the whole market is giddy and the options clock is running out.

wrong.The first day of a new rally: A market just starting a rally is the B- row. Climaxes end cycles.
wrong.A quiet market with no hype: No hype, no crowd to exhaust. The cue is euphoria.
wrong.A stock in week one out of a base: That is a pass on our card, not a grade cue.

questions.q: What was the mistake?
choices: Shorted strength: no crack, no burst
None; any gap up is a climax
The stop over the high was too tight
questions.answer: Shorted strength: no crack, no burst
questions.why: Shorting strength. The day closed above its open, so there was no crack, and one box is no burst. Shorting that close lost 4.5R on the next day's gap up.
questions.lesson_line: A green close with one box is strength. Shorting strength pays in R, the wrong way.

wrong.None; any gap up is a climax: A gap up that closes green has not cracked. The gap is the setup, the crack is the trigger.
wrong.The stop over the high was too tight: The stop was the rule's stop. The entry was the mistake: a green day with no burst.

questions.story: The stock gaps up 2.2% and closes 7.3% above its open. Only one burst box is checked. You short the close anyway.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Bracco: most climax points come at obvious ___ numbers.
questions.answer: round
questions.why: Round. Bracco: most of these climax points occur around very obvious, round numbers. A chart that looks parabolic even on a log scale is the strong form.
questions.lesson_line: Watch the big round number. Climaxes like a stage.

questions.q: Where was the error?
choices: Shorting week one out of a base
The stop over the high
Not holding past the new high
The 9 EMA target
questions.answer: Shorting week one out of a base
questions.why: Shorting a stock fresh out of a base. Bracco: very short lived if it set up. RGTI reached the 9 EMA on day 5 at 0.99R, then a new high on day 6 took the stop.
questions.lesson_line: Right candle, wrong week. A stock just out of a base has fuel.

wrong.The stop over the high: A few cents over the high is the rule. It did its job on day 6.
wrong.Not holding past the new high: Over the high you are wrong. Holding through it is the blow-up.
wrong.The 9 EMA target: The target was right and it was reached. The context was wrong.

questions.story: Fresh out of a base: two up days, then a 3.9% gap that closes red. You short 31.64, stop 34.44. Day 5 touches the 9 EMA at 0.99R; day 6 a new high takes the stop.

questions.q: Where should the short have been?
choices: At the VWAP break, after the turn
At the close; it is five stars
At the close, with a 3% stop
Nowhere; five-star climaxes are traps
questions.answer: At the VWAP break, after the turn
questions.why: At the VWAP break. On this climax the VWAP break at 90.01 ran 1.16R with the same stop. The short at the close, 34.3% from its stop, lost.
questions.lesson_line: The entry is the VWAP break after the turn. The close of a crash day is not it.

wrong.At the close; it is five stars: Five stars does not fix a 34.3% stop. If the honest stop does not fit, skip.
wrong.At the close, with a 3% stop: A stop inside the day's range is a stop pulled in to fit. You never do that.
wrong.Nowhere; five-star climaxes are traps: The setup was right. The entry at the close was the problem; the VWAP break worked.

questions.story: Bracco's five-star climax, four of four boxes. The day fell 34% from its high and closed at the low. A short at the close puts the stop 34.3% away.

questions.q: Kullamagi wants a smaller cap up 300% to 1,000% or more before he calls it a parabolic short candidate.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A stock up 50-100%+ in days or weeks if larger cap, or 300-1000%+ if smaller cap. Small caps need a far bigger run.
questions.lesson_line: The smaller the stock, the bigger the run it takes to exhaust.

questions.q: What rule capped the damage?
choices: The window and three tries a week
No rule; three losses is a mistake
The 2R gap ceiling
questions.answer: The window and three tries a week
questions.why: The 1 to 2 day window and the cap of 3 tries in a week. Bracco: 3 failed attempts over 2 sessions, no revenge trade, no averaging down. Then he dropped it.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries, no revenge, no adding. Then walk away.

wrong.No rule; three losses is a mistake: Three planned losses inside the window is the rule working. Revenge-shorting would be the mistake.
wrong.The 2R gap ceiling: No gap through the stop here. Each stop was taken in the session.

questions.story: Bracco shorted AGQ three times in two sessions and was stopped each time. He did not add and did not revenge trade.

questions.q: Is the short allowed under our 200-day rule?
choices: Yes; below the 200 needs no exception
No; a parabolic short must be above it
Only if the market is Red
questions.answer: Yes; below the 200 needs no exception
questions.why: Yes. Shorts are allowed below the 200-day as a matter of course; the parabolic exception is only needed above it.
questions.lesson_line: Below the 200-day a short needs no excuse. Above it, only the parabolic one.

wrong.No; a parabolic short must be above it: Nearly every climax sits far above its 200-day. Under it is the easy case, not a bar.
wrong.Only if the market is Red: The market reading is not what gates a short below the 200-day.

questions.story: A stock below its 200-day rips higher in a burst, then ends with a 6% gap up and a closing reversal.

questions.q: Short 48.50, stop 52.56. The stock gaps over the stop and the first 30-minute high is 53.40. How many R is the loss there?
questions.why: 1.21R. The 30-minute high minus the fill, over the stop minus the fill. Inside the 2R ceiling, so 53.40 is the new stop, not an exit.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap in R. Under 2R the 30-minute high is the stop; past it, you are out.

questions.q: Bracco: the climax day almost always shows the highest OPENING volume of the whole run.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Opening volume rises over several days, with the climax day almost invariably showing the highest opening volume of the entire run. Range and volume expansion come first.
questions.lesson_line: The biggest open of the run is the crowd arriving. That is who you sell to.

questions.q: Is it the climax-day short?
choices: No; no gap up that day
Yes; the red close is the crack
Yes; record volume is enough
questions.answer: No; no gap up that day
questions.why: No. The climax day must open above the prior close; Bracco won't short without that gap-up. A red close on record volume without the gap is not this trade.
questions.lesson_line: The gap is the exhaustion. Without it the day is just a red day.

wrong.Yes; the red close is the crack: The crack only counts after the gap. The gap is a required box.
wrong.Yes; record volume is enough: Volume grades the day. The gap is the gate.

questions.story: A four-day burst. Day five opens under the prior close, runs up, then closes red on record volume.

questions.q: What does the card teach from it?
choices: The time limit; the gap was small
Hold the five weeks; it paid 2.95R
A 2.8% gap is a strong A+ cue
questions.answer: The time limit; the gap was small
questions.why: The time limit, and a small gap grades lower. A 2.8% gap is the B- row; five weeks under the climax high breaks the 3-session rule. It paid 2.95R, but not by the plan.
questions.lesson_line: A climax that will not crack in three sessions is out of time. Cover and move on.

wrong.Hold the five weeks; it paid 2.95R: It got there, but five weeks under the high breaks the 3-session limit. That is not the plan.
wrong.A 2.8% gap is a strong A+ cue: A gap of 5% or more is the A+ cue. A small gap is the weak point.

questions.story: Four of four boxes and a close at the day's low, but the gap was 2.8%. Short 502.85, stop 547.76. The stock chops under its high for five weeks.

questions.q: Bracco's name for that, and his view of it?
choices: Quick opening range breakdown; weakest
The U-Turn; his favorite
A five-star climax
questions.answer: Quick opening range breakdown; weakest
questions.why: The Quick Opening Range Breakdown: the high set on the first 5-minute candle, then the opening range breaks. His least liked, and it often appears on day 1 or 2 of the burst.
questions.lesson_line: A top on the first candle of day two is usually not the top.

wrong.The U-Turn; his favorite: The U-Turn runs higher first and turns 10 to 60 minutes in. This topped on the first candle.
wrong.A five-star climax: Day two of a burst is early. The climax gap usually comes on day 3 to 5.

questions.story: Day two of a burst: two up days. Today it gaps up, sets its high on the first 5-minute candle and breaks the opening range low.

questions.q: Bracco: a frequent mistake is judging a stock by its percent gain alone and ignoring the chart's structure.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Relying solely on a stock's percentage gain, overlooking its chart structure and formation, is the mistake he names. A linear run, however far it has gone, is not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: The number gets you looking. The shape gets you the trade.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Out at once; past the 2R ceiling
New stop 74.00, the 30-minute high
Hold; it must come back to the 9 EMA
questions.answer: Out at once; past the 2R ceiling
questions.why: Out. The first 30 minutes decide, with a ceiling: past 2R, get out. Opening at 72.00 the loss is already 4R. This is the failure mode: a squeeze gaps up over the stop for 4R to 5R losses.
questions.lesson_line: The gap rule has a ceiling. Past 2R there is nothing to wait for.

wrong.New stop 74.00, the 30-minute high: The 30-minute high is the new stop only inside 2R. This gap is 4R at the open.
wrong.Hold; it must come back to the 9 EMA: Nothing must. A squeeze over the stop is the one way this setup blows up an account.

questions.story: You shorted the crack at 60.00, stop 63.00. Overnight news; it opens at 72.00 and the first 30-minute high is 74.00.

questions.q: Four boxes and record volume, but the climax gap is only 1.7%, like SCHW in 1999. Does the small gap rule it out?
choices: No; it passes, but the gap is weak
Yes; a gap under 5% is a pass
No; gap size does not matter at all
questions.answer: No; it passes, but the gap is weak
questions.why: No. It opened above the prior close, so it passes the gate; a small gap is a B- mark on our card. SCHW still reached the 9 EMA the next session.
questions.lesson_line: Any gap up passes the gate. A big one grades higher.

wrong.Yes; a gap under 5% is a pass: 5% is the A+ mark, not the gate. The gate is any open above the prior close.
wrong.No; gap size does not matter at all: It matters for the grade. A gap of 5% or more is the A+ row; a small one is a B- mark.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, target.
choices: Market now; stop over the high; 9 EMA
Short the open; stop 3%; cover at 3R
Wait for the close; stop at the 9 EMA
questions.answer: Market now; stop over the high; 9 EMA
questions.why: Market at the VWAP break, a few cents over the day's high, target the daily 9 EMA. GDS: short 48.50 on the daily stand-in, stop 52.56, the 9 EMA in 2 sessions, 3R on day 5.
questions.lesson_line: Entry at the turn, stop over the high, out at the 9 EMA. Write it before the open.

wrong.Short the open; stop 3%; cover at 3R: Nothing at the open, the stop is a level not a percent, and the target is the 9 EMA.
wrong.Wait for the close; stop at the 9 EMA: The close is a daily stand-in, not the trade. And the 9 EMA is below the price; it is the target.

questions.story: GDS, February 2025: a 13-session run from a flat base, four of four boxes, a 15.4% gap on record volume. On the 5-minute chart it runs, then breaks VWAP.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, after a burst; the last bar is the climax day. Did it gap up and close red? Take it or pass.
choices: Take it; a gap up that closed red
Pass; the day closed green, not red
Pass; there was no gap up today
questions.answer: Take it; a gap up that closed red
questions.why: Take it. A gap up that closed red after a 13-session run: four of four boxes, a 15% gap on record volume. It closed in the lower half; the 9 EMA came in 2 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Gap up, record volume, red close after a burst: that is the climax day.

wrong.Pass; the day closed green, not red: Look again: the last bar opened higher and closed lower, in the lower half of its range.
wrong.Pass; there was no gap up today: The last bar opened well above the prior close. The gap is there.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, after a burst; the last bar gapped up. Did it crack? Take it or pass.
choices: Pass; a green close, no crack
Take it; the gap is the trigger
Take it; volume is huge
questions.answer: Pass; a green close, no crack
questions.why: Pass. The day closed 15.8% above its open, at 95% of its range: a green climax day with no crack. The real top came the next day; a short at that close was stopped out the next session.
questions.lesson_line: A gap that never looks back has not cracked. Wait for the red one.

wrong.Take it; the gap is the trigger: The gap is the setup. The crack is the trigger, and this bar closed near its high.
wrong.Take it; volume is huge: Volume grades a climax that cracked. This one has not cracked yet.

questions.q: By the card?
choices: Drop the idea; the window has passed
Short again; three tries are allowed
Short again, at half size
questions.answer: Drop the idea; the window has passed
questions.why: Drop it. A 1 to 2 day window: if the trigger fails twice or the window passes, drop the idea. Stamatoudis: if it doesn't work out, he skips the setup altogether.
questions.lesson_line: Two tries in two days and nothing. The idea is over; obsessing over it is the mistake.

wrong.Short again; three tries are allowed: Three a week is the outer cap. The window rule drops it after two failures or two days.
wrong.Short again, at half size: Half size on a dead idea is half a mistake.

questions.story: The climax came Monday. Tuesday and Wednesday both triggers failed. Thursday it sets up again.

questions.q: In our scan of climax-day shorts, more than one in three reached 3R before the stop.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Only 18.8% reached 3R and 12.5% reached 5R before the stop. This setup is paid at the 9 EMA, inside a few sessions, or not at all.
questions.lesson_line: Do not wait for 3R on this setup. The 9 EMA is the target.

questions.q: What does Bracco say about it?
choices: Still viable, with that expansion
Not viable; three up days or none
Skip it; two days is another setup
Viable only after a third up day
questions.answer: Still viable, with that expansion
questions.why: Still viable. With only two up days, Bracco keeps it a candidate if the move shows significant price and ATR expansion. Our card allows this two-day exception only with big expansion.
questions.lesson_line: Two up days can work, but only with big expansion.

wrong.Not viable; three up days or none: Bracco says not every box needs to be satisfied, and he gives this very case.
wrong.Skip it; two days is another setup: He calls it a viable candidate when the two days show big price and ATR expansion.
wrong.Viable only after a third up day: Waiting for a third day is not his rule. The expansion in the two days is the test.

questions.story: A stock rose only two days in a row before a climax-day gap up. Those two days showed sharp price and ATR expansion.

questions.q: Why does Bracco steer you away from a steady, linear ascent?
choices: It shows strength and can persist
It always ends in a sharp gap down
It has too little volume to measure
It trades under the 200-day line
questions.answer: It shows strength and can persist
